goal: Deepen the quick-pick-survey flagship with a feature that reduces the number of pairwise picks a long list needs, without making the stop rule claim more than it delivers.
notes: Simulation (scripts/pile-first.mjs, page's own loop, same people and coins both arms): ordinary answerers at 20 options: no sort 93 actions (Spearman 0.933), careful sort 64 (0.929), ordinary 87 (0.937), careless 120 (0.933). Close calls careful sort: 86 vs 135 (20 options), 96 vs 253 (30). Two fixes found by the simulation before shipping: pile-aware own-prior check (with the old check, half of perfect-pile runs hit the cap) and check pairs every 4th pick (without them, close-call people's stop claimed 0.90 for true 0.79). Checks: node --test site/*.test.mjs 103 pass; vitest 575 pass; tsc clean; eslint 0 errors; Playwright at 390 px clean. run_venture_tests.py quick-pick-survey: ok. venture-preflight: first run failed on my own post front matter (seo_title 73, description 162) and the new script's CLI entry check (file:// string); both fixed, second run 'preflight clean for quick-pick-survey'.
